W5 (contrarian), after E017.
1. Noise is the main fact, and it is larger than I thought. E017 was a graph-break cleanup with "identical math", and the 3-seed mean fell from 0.7607 to 0.7537 (−0.70 pp). E015 vs E010, another identical-math pair, moved +0.27 pp. A re-run of the same binary is bit-identical (E012). Any change to kernels, graphs or RNG consumption is effectively a fresh 3-seed draw. I now put the 3-seed SD at about 0.25 pp, with per-seed SD of about 0.4 pp. Effects under about 0.4 pp (LS, Muon lr, LR→0, and the E016 WD halving) are not separable from noise. My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.756–0.757: E015, E016 and E017 average 0.7573, and the keep decisions add a winner's-curse discount. So the tip sits about 1 SD above the 0.753 bar locally and has roughly 0.6 pp headroom over the 0.75 official bar. Most trims that cost ≥0.3 pp will land under 0.753 on a typical draw, even though the true 40-seed mean would stay above 0.75.
2. A mechanism nobody has named for the E016→E017 swing: E017 may have changed the RNG stream (for example, the order of augment, randperm and flip_mask, or a GPU-tensor LR path), not just kernels. The swing is about 2.5σ for a pure kernel reshuffle. That makes it either an unlucky draw or a subtle, real behaviour change: the LR or whitening-bias schedule could now be applied differently inside compiled or cudagraph regions, for example a stale LR captured in a graph. I'd want a diff-level check that each step's LR equals schedule[step] in E017.
3. What the code settles: Muon renormalizes filters every step, applies no WD, and already uses 3 Newton-Schulz steps. So the filter WD is inert, H1.5.4 is trivially true, and E016's effect (if real) came from the SGD groups: the head, which sets logit temperature with ×1/9 and LS 0.3, and the BN biases. The true step count is ceil(9.5×25) = 238, which is 9.5 epochs.
4. Where accuracy comes from: averaging (E005, about +1 pp), Muon plus batch 2000 (E006, +0.66 pp), and the share of the final phase at 32 px. In E011, cutting the 32 px tail cost about 1.4 pp. Low-resolution phases are cheap in accuracy, but each one saves little time.
5. Time is GPU FLOPs. Per-step pixel cost at 20/24/28/32 px is 0.39 : 0.56 : 0.77 : 1. Conv MACs at 32 px split roughly 18/49/33% across group 1/2/3. Fixed overhead (prepare, whitening, transfer) is about 0.4–0.6 s and does not shrink. Systems levers are exhausted: CUDA graphs and graph-break removal each gave under 1%. Time noise is about ±1%.
6. Lookahead on Muon's sphere does angular damping, and the BN buffers are averaged consistently with the weights. Recomputing BN statistics should gain nothing, because BN momentum 0.4 already tracks the final 32 px phase.
Unsure: the held-out mean; whether E017's drop is real; whether any single trim (28→24, or group 2 → 320) costs under 0.3 pp.

forecasts.reason: Saves about 8% of train FLOPs. Replacing 28 px with 24 px costs about 0.2–0.4 pp, which is inside a reshuffle of ±0.25.
Same binary, so the reported values should repeat the tip. I expect the 10-seed mean at about 0.7565, more than 0.3 pp below 0.7607.
−1.0 true epoch costs about 10% of time and 0.4–0.8 pp. Only one point of the two-point test is run, and on a noisy base.
Removes about 15% of MACs, which is about 7% of time. Capacity loss on 100 classes is about 0.4 pp against the E016 baseline.
Filter WD is inert. Any small head-temperature gain is swamped by a reshuffle, and beating E016 by 0.2 pp (0.7627) is unlikely.
Group 1's third conv is about 6.5% of MACs plus memory-bound elementwise work, so time falls about 6%. Losing depth at the start likely costs about 0.5 pp.
Going 24→20 px on 15% of steps saves only about 3% of compute, under the 4% bar. The accuracy cost is small.

cruxes: Was E017's −0.7 pp a pure reshuffle, or did the graph-break cleanup change behaviour (RNG order, or a stale LR or whitening-bias schedule inside compiled or cudagraph regions)? Check by logging each step's LR and by comparing E016 and E017 per-seed results on held-out seeds.
What is the tip's held-out 10-seed mean? If it is ≥0.757, there is room for one ~0.3 pp trim; if it is about 0.754, no trim can pass the 3-seed bar except by luck.
Of the cheap time levers (28→24 px, group 2 → 320, dropping group 1's third conv), which has the best seconds-per-pp ratio when measured with multi-seed means rather than single 3-seed draws?
